questions.knowledgeNote: A polynomial is continuous everywhere, so the limit is just the value: substitute x = a.
questions.question: Q1(a). Find the limit: lim (x→2) (2x² + 3x − 14).
questions.solution: 2x² + 3x − 14 is a polynomial, hence continuous at x = 2. Substitute: 2(2)² + 3(2) − 14 = 8 + 6 − 14 = 0. Boxed 0 (matches the printed key, book p466).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q1(a); book p465 = PDF p492 (vision read); key book p466 = PDF p493

questions.knowledgeNote: Same substitution rule for any polynomial.
questions.question: Q1(b). Find the limit: lim (x→5) (x² + 2x − 9).
questions.solution: Polynomial → direct substitution: (5)² + 2(5) − 9 = 25 + 10 − 9 = 26. Boxed 26 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q1(b); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Quotient of polynomials: substitute, provided the denominator is non-zero.
questions.question: Q1(c). Find the limit: lim (x→1) (3x² + 2x − 4)/(x² + 5x − 4).
questions.solution: Denominator at x = 1: 1 + 5 − 4 = 2 ≠ 0, so substitute directly: numerator 3 + 2 − 4 = 1, denominator 2. Value = 1/2. Boxed 1/2 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q1(c); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Check the denominator first: if it is non-zero at the point, just substitute.
questions.question: Q1(d). Find the limit: lim (x→3) (6x² + 3x − 12)/(2x² + x + 1).
questions.solution: At x = 3: numerator 6(9) + 9 − 12 = 54 + 9 − 12 = 51; denominator 2(9) + 3 + 1 = 22 ≠ 0. Value = 51/22. Boxed 51/22 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q1(d); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: 0/0 form: cancel the common factor x (x ≠ 0 on the approach).
questions.question: Q2(a). Compute: lim (x→0) (4x³ − x² + 2x)/(3x² + 4x).
questions.solution: At x = 0 both numerator and denominator vanish (0/0 form). Factor: numerator = x(4x² − x + 2), denominator = x(3x + 4). For x ≠ 0 cancel x: (4x² − x + 2)/(3x + 4). Now substitute x = 0: 2/4 = 1/2. Boxed 1/2 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(a); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: x³ − a³ = (x − a)(x² + ax + a²) and x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a): cancel (x − 4).
questions.question: Q2(b). Compute: lim (x→4) (x³ − 64)/(x² − 16).
questions.solution: 0/0 at x = 4. Factor: x³ − 64 = (x − 4)(x² + 4x + 16); x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4). For x ≠ 4 cancel (x − 4): (x² + 4x + 16)/(x + 4). Substitute x = 4: (16 + 16 + 16)/8 = 48/8 = 6. Boxed 6 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(b); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Treat x^(2/3) as (x^(1/3))², difference of squares, then x − a = (x^(1/3))³ − (a^(1/3))³.
questions.question: Q2(c). Compute: lim (x→a) (x^(2/3) − a^(2/3))/(x − a).
questions.solution: Put u = x^(1/3), c = a^(1/3) (so u³ = x, c³ = a). The quotient becomes (u² − c²)/(u³ − c³) = (u − c)(u + c)/[(u − c)(u² + uc + c²)] = (u + c)/(u² + uc + c²) for u ≠ c. As x → a, u → c: (c + c)/(3c²) = 2c/(3c²) = 2/(3c) = (2/3)a^(−1/3). Boxed (2/3)a^(−1/3) (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(c); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: x² + 3x − 4 = (x + 4)(x − 1): cancel the vanishing factor.
questions.question: Q2(d). Compute: lim (x→1) (x² + 3x − 4)/(x − 1).
questions.solution: Numerator at x = 1 is 0, denominator 0. Factor: x² + 3x − 4 = (x + 4)(x − 1). Cancel (x − 1) for x ≠ 1: limit = lim (x + 4) = 5. Boxed 5 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(d); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Factorise top and bottom; the (x − 2) factor cancels.
questions.question: Q2(e). Compute: lim (x→2) (x² − 5x + 6)/(x² − x − 2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(e); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: If the numerator vanishes to a higher order, the limit is 0 — but only after cancelling the common factor.
questions.question: Q2(f). Compute: lim (x→2) (x² − 4x + 4)/(x² − 7x + 10).
questions.solution: x² − 4x + 4 = (x − 2)²; x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 2)(x − 5). Cancel one (x − 2): (x − 2)/(x − 5) → 0/(2 − 5) = 0. Boxed 0 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(f); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: √A − √B forms: multiply by the conjugate (√A + √B); the difference of squares frees the (x − a) factor.
questions.question: Q2(g). Compute: lim (x→a) (√(3x) − √(2x + a))/(2(x − a)).
questions.solution: At x = a: √(3a) − √(3a) = 0 (0/0 form). Rationalise the numerator: √(3x) − √(2x + a) = [3x − (2x + a)]/[√(3x) + √(2x + a)] = (x − a)/[√(3x) + √(2x + a)]. Therefore the quotient = 1/{2[√(3x) + √(2x + a)]} (for x ≠ a). As x → a: 1/[2(√(3a) + √(3a))] = 1/(4√(3a)). Boxed 1/(4√(3a)) (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(g); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalise BOTH square-root differences; the (x − a) factors cancel and a minus sign survives.
questions.question: Q2(h). Compute: lim (x→a) (√(2x) − √(3x − a))/(√x − √a). [T.U. 2053 H]
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(h); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: After rationalising, x² + 2x − 3 = (x − 1)(x + 3) supplies the cancelling factor.
questions.question: Q2(i). Compute: lim (x→1) (√(2x) − √(3 − x²))/(x − 1).
questions.solution: At x = 1: √2 − √2 = 0, and the denominator is 0 (0/0 form). Rationalise: √(2x) − √(3 − x²) = [2x − (3 − x²)]/[√(2x) + √(3 − x²)] = (x² + 2x − 3)/[√(2x) + √(3 − x²)] = (x − 1)(x + 3)/[√(2x) + √(3 − x²)]. Cancel (x − 1): limit = (1 + 3)/(√2 + √2) = 4/(2√2) = √2. Boxed √2 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(i); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: x − (6 − x²) = (x − 2)(x + 3): the conjugate frees a factor (x − 2).
questions.question: Q2(j). Compute: lim (x→2) (√x − √(6 − x²))/(x − 2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(j); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Two different roots of the same x: substitute u = x^(1/6) to turn both into powers of one variable.
questions.question: Q2(k). Compute: lim (x→64) (⁶√x − 2)/(³√x − 4).
questions.solution: Put u = x^(1/6), so x = u⁶, ⁶√x = u and ³√x = x^(1/3) = u². As x → 64, u → 2. Quotient = (u − 2)/(u² − 4) = (u − 2)/[(u − 2)(u + 2)] = 1/(u + 2) (u ≠ 2) → 1/4. Boxed 1/4 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(k); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: The conjugate gives (3a − x) − (x + a) = −2(x − a), which cancels the (x − a) in the denominator.
questions.question: Q2(l). Compute: lim (x→a) (√(3a − x) − √(x + a))/(4(x − a)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q2(l); book p465 = PDF p492; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Limit at infinity of a rational function: divide by the highest power of x; only the leading coefficients survive.
questions.question: Q3(a). Calculate: lim (x→∞) 2x²/(3x² + 2).
questions.solution: Divide numerator and denominator by x²: 2/(3 + 2/x²). As x → ∞, 2/x² → 0, so the limit is 2/3. Boxed 2/3 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q3(a); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal degrees → ratio of leading coefficients.
questions.question: Q3(b). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (3x² − 4)/(4x²).
questions.solution: Divide by x²: (3 − 4/x²)/4 → 3/4 as x → ∞. Boxed 3/4 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q3(b); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Lower-order terms are negligible at infinity; compare 4x² with 5x².
questions.question: Q3(c). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (4x² + 3x + 2)/(5x² + 4x − 3).
questions.solution: Divide by x²: (4 + 3/x + 2/x²)/(5 + 4/x − 3/x²). Every term with 1/x or 1/x² → 0, leaving 4/5. Boxed 4/5 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q3(c); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Same degree on both sides: the ratio of leading coefficients is the limit.
questions.question: Q3(d). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (5x² + 2x − 7)/(3x² + 5x + 2).
questions.solution: Divide by x²: (5 + 2/x − 7/x²)/(3 + 5/x + 2/x²) → 5/3. Boxed 5/3 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q3(d); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: ∞ − ∞ form: rationalise. A fixed difference inside the roots gives 0 because the conjugate grows like 2√x.
questions.question: Q4(a). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (√x − √(x − 3)).
questions.solution: Multiply by the conjugate: (x − (x − 3))/(√x + √(x − 3)) = 3/[√x + √(x − 3)]. As x → ∞ the denominator → ∞, so the quotient → 0. Boxed 0 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q4(a); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Same argument for constants a, b: the numerator becomes the constant (b − a).
questions.question: Q4(b). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (√(x − a) − √(x − b)). [T.U. 2048 H]
questions.solution: Conjugate: [(x − a) − (x − b)]/[√(x − a) + √(x − b)] = (b − a)/[√(x − a) + √(x − b)] → (b − a)/∞ = 0. Boxed 0 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q4(b); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Here the two square-root terms have different growth (√(3x) vs √x), so the difference diverges.
questions.question: Q4(c). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (√(3x) − √(x − 5)).
questions.solution: Conjugate: [(3x) − (x − 5)]/[√(3x) + √(x − 5)] = (2x + 5)/[√(3x) + √(x − 5)]. Divide top and bottom by √x: (2√x + 5/√x)/(√3 + √(1 − 5/x)) → (2√x)/√3 → ∞. Equivalently √(3x) − √x = (√3 − 1)√x → ∞. Boxed ∞ (matches the key; the printed note adds that an infinite limit means the limit does not exist).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q4(c); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: √x·(√x − √(x − a)) = a√x/(√x + √(x − a)): divide by √x to see the a/2.
questions.question: Q4(d). Calculate: lim (x→∞) √x(√x − √(x − a)). [T.U. 2052]
questions.solution: Inside: √x − √(x − a) = [x − (x − a)]/[√x + √(x − a)] = a/[√x + √(x − a)]. Multiply by √x: a√x/[√x + √(x − a)]. Divide numerator and denominator by √x: a/[1 + √(1 − a/x)] → a/(1 + 1) = a/2. Boxed a/2 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q4(d); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: With a coefficient b on the second root the growth rates differ: equality b = 1 is the only case that cancels.
questions.question: Q4(e). Calculate: lim (x→∞) (√(x − a) − √(bx)).
questions.solution: Conjugate: [(x − a) − bx]/[√(x − a) + √(bx)] = [(1 − b)x − a]/[√(x − a) + √(bx)]. For b = 1 the numerator is the constant −a, so the quotient → 0. For b ≠ 1 divide by √x: [(1 − b)√x − a/√x]/[√(1 − a/x) + √b] → (1 − b)√x/(1 + √b). This is +∞ when 0 < b < 1, and −∞ when b > 1 (the printed key states ∞ for b ≠ 1 and reminds that an infinite limit means the limit does not exist). Boxed 0 if b = 1; ∞ (i.e. no finite limit) if b ≠ 1 (matches the key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q4(e); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Double rationalisation: each 0/0 difference of squares yields the same (x² − 4), which cancels.
questions.question: Q5(a). Evaluate: lim (x→2) (x − √(8 − x²))/(√(x² + 12) − 4).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q5(a); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466

questions.knowledgeNote: Both conjugates reduce to 2(x² − 1), so the factors cancel and the limit is the ratio of the remaining sums.
questions.question: Q5(b). Evaluate: lim (x→1) (x − √(2 − x²))/(2x − √(2 + 2x²)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.16 Ex 16.1 Q5(b); book p466 = PDF p493; key book p466
